title: Chocolate Mousse
description: The essence of a mousse is lightness, indicated by its French name meaning foam or froth. This favourite is delicate yet rich with cream and chocolate.

method.instruction: Place chocolate in a heatproof bowl set over a pan of simmering water. Stir until melted, then remove from heat.
Add butter and stir until melted. Stir in egg yolks one at a time. Transfer mixture to a large bowl, cover, and allow to cool.
Beat egg whites in a small bowl with an electric mixer until medium soft peaks form. Do not over-whip or the mousse will become grainy.
Whip the cream until soft peaks form. Do not over-mix — the butter is already providing richness.
Gently fold cream and egg whites alternately, a third at a time, into the cooled chocolate mixture until just combined.
Pour or spoon into serving dishes, cover with plastic wrap, and refrigerate overnight.

notes.title: Egg Whites
notes.content: Do not over-whip the egg whites or the mousse will have a grainy texture. Stop when medium soft peaks form — they should hold their shape but still look glossy and moist.

notes.title: Microwave Option
notes.content: Chocolate and butter can be melted together in the microwave. Heat in 30-second bursts, stirring between each, until smooth.

notes.title: Serving Tip
notes.content: Serve with extra whipped cream and chocolate curls if desired.

notes.title: Storage
notes.content: Keep covered in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Not suitable for freezing.

notes.title: Recipe Source
notes.content: Adapted from The Australian Women's Weekly Home Library — Sweet Old-Fashioned Favourites, page 34.
